subject: Transportation Systems
title: Wind Shear
description: A quick win: understand Wind Shear.

hook.text: Wind shear is a sudden change in wind speed or direction. It strikes hardest during takeoff and landing.

buildup.text: A plane on approach expects steady headwind. If wind suddenly shifts to tailwind, airspeed drops fast.

discovery.text: Lost airspeed means lost lift. The plane sinks faster than the pilot expects—sometimes fatally.

twist.text: Microbursts—columns of air slamming downward from storms—are the most dangerous form of wind shear.

climax.text: Modern aircraft have wind shear detection systems that warn pilots seconds before impact.

punchline.text: Wind shear is invisible, instant, and lethal near the ground.

quiz.question: What is a microburst?
options: A column of air slamming downward from a storm
